    Orientation

    Who should read this. Readers beginning Orabona Chapter 1; all declarations share the canonical Lean graph.

    Learning goals

    • Distinguish the actual past-only prediction from a hindsight leader.
    • Derive the logarithmic regret bound from actual mean updates.
    • Distinguish arbitrary deterministic loss sequences from IID expectation guarantees.

    Textbook crosswalk

    Read the mathematics before the Lean interface

    This reading follows Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization. Teaching routes group mathematical dependencies across the shared library. Visible page labels use the cited source's numbered pages; source buttons use the PDF viewer's physical page index, including front matter. Companion papers cover algorithm-specific results.

    Notation you will meet

    x_t
    Actual prediction before target t; source initial choice is 1/2.
    x_t*
    Hindsight mean through target t; not the prediction at round t.
    Regret / expected excess
    Deterministic best-fixed regret and stochastic variance-relative excess are distinct quantities.
    strict-past empirical mean · ordered flow

    Follow-the-Leader for squared guessing loss

    Read top to bottom: each step supplies the state or proof fact used by the next one.

    1. 01
      Initialize

      Predict one half before seeing the first target.

    2. 02
      Predict

      On later rounds, output the average of all previous targets.

    3. 03
      Observe

      Pay squared error and update the running average with the current target.

    Worked example · follow one decision

    Two targets: zero, then one

    Use the actual source initial prediction 1/2 and strict-past mean.

    1. 01
      First prediction

      Predict 1/2, observe zero, and pay 1/4.

      Worked example step 1. Formula renderer unavailable; readable fallback: First loss is one quarter.x1=1/2,ℓ1(x1)=1/4.Swipe to read the full formula →
    2. 02
      Second prediction

      Predict zero, observe one, and pay one. The best fixed mean is one half.

      Worked example step 2. Formula renderer unavailable; readable fallback: The actual regret is three quarters.x2=0,x2∗=1/2,R2=3/4.Swipe to read the full formula →
    3. 03
      Compare cumulative losses

      The actual strategy pays 5/4; the optimal fixed mean pays 1/2. Their difference is 3/4.

      Worked example step 3. Formula renderer unavailable; readable fallback: Cumulative regret is three quarters.R2=5/4−1/2=3/4.Swipe to read the full formula →

    Takeaway. The hindsight leader and causal predictor differ; the exact positive regret is checked in Lean.

    Lemma 1.2: Be-the-Leader

    Original at printed p. 4 ↗
    Existing Be-the-Leader: current source/body revalidationExisting Lemma 1.2 has been rechecked with seven named validation proofs. It compares supplied feasible hindsight minimizers; it does not construct a causal learner or establish a regret rate. The arbitrary-type extension and horizon boundaries are explained below. This bounded package does not complete Chapter 1 or its integration into main.

    Prefix minimizers beat the final fixed leader in cumulative loss.

    Model
    Source V is a subset of real Euclidean space and losses are real on V. The public lemma generalizes to arbitrary ambient type X and total real loss functions; restriction to V recovers the source, and outside-V values are unused when leaders are feasible. No geometry, convexity, compactness or probability premise is required.
    Assumptions
    For EVERY positive prefix n<=T, supplied leader n lies in V and minimizes the prefix sum against EVERY u in V. Both membership and prefix argmin are premises; minimizer existence is not constructed. For T>0 this data implies V inhabited; T0 is a vacuous empty-sum extension with no condition on leader0.
    Algorithm parameters
    Source loss ell_(t+1) is Lean loss t; source x*_n is leader n. Lean diagonal uses leader(t+1) over rangeT; the fixed comparison uses leaderT. T1 has identical sides. Existing induction cancels the final summand, applies the previous prefix inequality, then uses prefix argmin with the feasible next/final leader.
    Regret notion
    A deterministic cumulative-loss comparison between auxiliary hindsight prefix leaders and the final leader; no regret rate or expectation conclusion.
    Guarantee
    The auxiliary hindsight leader at prefix n includes the current loss. It is NOT the causal FTL prediction, which uses the strict past. Lemma1.2 alone produces no learner, no-regret/logarithmic rate, stochastic expectation or minimax theorem. Teaching links to those later results are not actual proof dependencies of this lemma. Actual changing Bool canary: false always costs0, true costs-2 then3, feasible prefix leaders true thenfalse. It produces all prefix argmins and proves diagonal-2 versus final0, hence STRICT -2<0. Keeping feasible leaders false thentrue violates prefix optimality (-2<0 at prefix1) and reverses comparison3>1. Separately, ambient losses true:-10 then5 / false:0 with V={false} and leaders false thentrue satisfy ALL prefix comparisons against V, but finalleader lies outside V and reverse comparison5>-5. This is an ambient-extension test showing the necessity of feasibility, not an admissible trajectory for a source loss defined only on V. Empty/one-horizon boundary tests are separate named proofs.

    Theorem 1.3: guessing with the past mean

    Original at printed p. 4 ↗
    Existing FTL chain, two proof bounds exposedCompiled local proof package; chapter acceptance and main integration remain separate. The arbitrary-initial FTL family and a minimax lower bound are not established by these two bounds.

    The actual history-mean predictor achieves the source logarithmic regret bound.

    Model
    Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. The predictor uses exactly the targets already observed: first prediction 1/2, then their empirical mean. Empty-prefix mean0 is bookkeeping and differs from the first prediction.
    Assumptions
    Positive horizon T; every target in its finite prefix belongs to [0,1]. There is no probability or global future-boundedness premise.
    Algorithm parameters
    Source rounds1..T are Lean indices0..T-1. The tail range(T-1) has real denominators t+2>0 and is empty at T=1.
    Regret notion
    Cumulative squared loss minus the same final empirical-mean minimizer loss.
    Guarantee
    The existing4+4logT theorem is retained. The proof now separately exposes its initial1/4 estimate and exact later harmonic tail.

    Theorem 1.3 proof: initial1/4 stability

    Original at printed p.5 (unnumbered proof bound) ↗
    New source-bound proof compiled locallyCompiled local proof package; chapter acceptance and main integration remain separate. The arbitrary-initial FTL family and a minimax lower bound are not established by these two bounds.

    After observing the first target, its hindsight mean is that target, so the second squared loss is zero. The interval bounds imply y1(1-y1)>=0, which bounds the initial squared error by1/4.

    Model
    Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. The predictor uses exactly the targets already observed: first prediction 1/2, then their empirical mean. Empty-prefix mean0 is bookkeeping and differs from the first prediction.
    Assumptions
    Only the first target belongs to [0,1]. Future targets are unrestricted.
    Algorithm parameters
    Only source round1 is involved: x1=1/2 maps to meanPredict y0; the one-observation hindsight leader x1*=y1 maps to empiricalMean y1=y0. This statement has no horizon or tail parameter.
    Regret notion
    Actual initial stability loss difference.
    Guarantee
    The one-observation hindsight mean is the first target, so its squared loss is zero. Only y0 in [0,1] is needed to bound the initial squared error by 1/4. Targets 0 and 1 attain 1/4, target 1/2 yields 0, and target 2 gives 9/4 outside the theorem domain. This first-round estimate makes no assertion about feasibility of later means when future targets are unrestricted.

    Be-the-Leader compares the produced prefix minimizers with the final mean. Subtract these losses from the actual prediction losses, split off the first round, and add its1/4 estimate to the existing4/t bounds for later rounds.

    Model
    Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. The predictor uses exactly the targets already observed: first prediction 1/2, then their empirical mean. Empty-prefix mean0 is bookkeeping and differs from the first prediction.
    Assumptions
    Positive horizon T; every target in its finite prefix belongs to [0,1]. There is no probability or global future-boundedness premise.

    Source rounds1..T are Lean indices0..T-1. The tail range(T-1) has real denominators t+2>0 and is empty at T=1.

    Actual predictor loss minus the produced best-fixed mean loss.
    Guarantee
    Be-the-Leader compares the produced prefix minimizers with the final mean. Subtract these losses from the actual prediction losses, split off the first round, and add its1/4 estimate to the existing4/t bounds for later rounds. The final empirical mean is proved feasible and globally minimizing, so its loss is the source best-fixed minimum over [0,1]. Prefix leaders are produced for Be-the-Leader; hindsight leaders are auxiliary, while predictions use the strict past. The initial loss difference equals1/4 at targets0 and1, and0 at1/2. Target2 gives9/4 and lies outside the theorem domain. For targets0,1 the actual two-round regret is3/4 while the displayed bound is9/4. Changing the current unseen target leaves the prefix prediction unchanged.

    FTL family and actual mean/count state

    Original at printed pp.3,6; structural source obligations, not a numbered theorem ↗
    Two producer obligations closed locally; chapter openCompiled local BODY-approved package. Combined project, reader FINAL, native acceptance and PR delivery are separate pending gates. No new regret rate for arbitrary c. The first-round quarter and the prior refined/logarithmic theorem remain specific to c=1/2. The state is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair (count,value). The count grows; there is no fixed-bit memory, executable implementation or runtime certificate. Strict-prefix equality compares the same fixed c and gives no causality guarantee if an external caller chooses c from future data.

    The all-time mean successor identity has positive real denominator t+1. At t=0 the empty empirical mean is0 but the actual prediction is c. The first recursive update cancels c and gives (1,y0). For t>0 induction and the proved mean successor identity give the complete state identity. Existing decomposition, minimization and uniqueness prove the positive-prefix mean is the actual hindsight squared-loss leader; interval feasibility makes it an admissible comparator. The prediction uses the previous prefix, rather than an argmin or state oracle.

    Model
    Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. Fix initial c before observations. Lean time t counts observed labels y0,...,y(t-1); predict before observing yt, then update the local state with yt.
    Assumptions
    The algebraic identities hold for all real initial values and labels. Source feasibility requires c in [0,1] and only the strict-past labels yi in [0,1] for i<t; the current and future labels are unrestricted.
    Algorithm parameters
    The state is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair (count,value). The count grows; there is no fixed-bit memory, executable implementation or runtime certificate. Strict-prefix equality compares the same fixed c and gives no causality guarantee if an external caller chooses c from future data.
    Regret notion
    The exact half specialization connects this same recursive trajectory to existing source regret bounds. Arbitrary c has no new quarter or rate theorem here.
    Guarantee
    The all-time mean successor identity has positive real denominator t+1. At t=0 the empty empirical mean is0 but the actual prediction is c. The first recursive update cancels c and gives (1,y0). For t>0 induction and the proved mean successor identity give the complete state identity. Existing decomposition, minimization and uniqueness prove the positive-prefix mean is the actual hindsight squared-loss leader; interval feasibility makes it an admissible comparator. The prediction uses the previous prefix, rather than an argmin or state oracle. Six public canaries check distinct initial states and their identical first update; varying means1/2 and2/3; unchanged prediction before a changed current target and changed next state; feasible initial1 and outside-initial2 at time0; the half-state two-round regret3/4 with the prior bound; and feasible initial1,target0 giving first loss1>1/4.     Subtract the two finite loss sums and distribute subtraction termwise using Mathlib Finset.sum_sub_distrib. For the adapter, tendsto_order makes a comparator-wise bound tending tozero less than any positive epsilon eventually; intersect this event with the supplied actual normalized-regret upper bound and use transitivity. The adapter does not itself construct that bound. The typed illustrative game has V=[0,1],W=[0,2], constant output2 and loss_t(x)=-x onW. The actual shared adapter applies with bound0. At T2 the same output gives regret -4 against0 and -2 against1. This is a generalized negative-regret test, separate from the source squared guessing game and no universal W performance claim.

    Model
    Losses are defined on W, predictions belong to W, and fixed comparators belong to V⊆W. Lean uses X=Subtype W and comparator set {w:Subtype W | w.val∈V}; inclusion embeds a subtype-V comparator without changing its value. The source uses finite-dimensional Euclidean vectors; the shared algebraic API explicitly generalizes the carrier. Footnote1 states a modelling possibility, not a generic algorithm or performance theorem.
    Assumptions
    Only inclusion V⊆W is needed for the embedding. Finite regret algebra needs no convexity, compactness, probability or nonnegativity. A supplied prediction sequence is shared across every comparator. Its loss-prefix evaluation identity does not prove causal learner recomputation, future independence or existence of a best comparator. A W-loss restricts to V by pullback; a V-only loss is never evaluated outside V.
    Algorithm parameters
    Source round1 is Lean0; sums use range T. At T0 both sums are empty; Lean real division is total. Eventual atTop bounds concern sufficiently large positive horizons. Empty comparator sets give a vacuous property; supplied subtype inhabitants do not prove arbitrary sets are nonempty.
    Regret notion
    NoRegret means, for each fixed feasible comparator u and every positive epsilon, normalized regret is eventually at most epsilon. The threshold may depend on u and epsilon. This is an explicit interpretation of the source displayed ordinary-limit inequality: it agrees when the ordinary limit exists, but proves no ordinary limit existence, convergence tozero, absolute bound, nonnegative regret or uniform comparator threshold.
    Guarantee
    Subtract the two finite loss sums and distribute subtraction termwise using Mathlib Finset.sum_sub_distrib. For the adapter, tendsto_order makes a comparator-wise bound tending tozero less than any positive epsilon eventually; intersect this event with the supplied actual normalized-regret upper bound and use transitivity. The adapter does not itself construct that bound. The typed illustrative game has V=[0,1],W=[0,2], constant output2 and loss_t(x)=-x onW. For every comparator u∈V, each actual loss gap is u-2≤-1≤0; Finset.sum_nonpos and div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg make its finite sum and normalized regret nonpositive. The actual shared adapter applies with bound0. At T2 the same output gives regret -4 against0 and -2 against1. This is a generalized negative-regret test, separate from the source squared guessing game and no universal W performance claim.     Actual recursive normalization gives E_T[K]=T/2 and E_T[K²]=T(2T+1)/6, hence E_T[q(1-q)]=(T+3)/(6(T+2)). Causal prefix identities generate the actual same-path cumulative learner-loss successor. Conditional square loss is at least q(1-q), so summing its actual expected increments gives learner loss at least T/6+(H(T+1)-1)/6. The shared empirical mean is proved feasible and globally minimizes the same binary path square loss; its produced expected optimum is (T-1)/6. Subtracting these same-path quantities proves E_T[R_A]≥H(T+1)/6 for any real strict-history policy. For bounded measurable seed policies, proved integrability permits finite weighted sum/integral interchange. Strictly positive normalized path weights imply some ONE path has seed-average regret at least H(T+1)/6. Mathlib log_add_one_le_harmonic gives the log endpoint. These are actual compiled proof dependencies, separate from the curated teaching route.

    Model
    Histories h are newest-first binary lists. K(h) counts true labels; q(h)=(K(h)+1)/(|h|+2), w([])=1 and w(b::h)=w(h)*(q(h) if b=true else1-q(h)). This same normalized positive binary law depends on neither learner policy nor seed. Normalization and nonnegativity are proved before constructing the shared finite-action probability measure and integral. The chronological stream is reverse(h); padding beyond its length is never used by regret. The prediction at Lean round t receives reverse of the chronological strict prefix of length t. The current label is revealed after prediction. Source round1 is Lean0.
    Assumptions
    For every measurable seed space Ω, every probability measure μ, every policy A:Ω→List Bool→ℝ with each history section ω↦A(ω,h) measurable and A(ω,h)∈[0,1] for every seed and every history, and every positive natural horizon T, the terminal produces ONE binary vector v of length T outside the seed integral. The seed may encode the full private random tape; each policy remains strict-past. The integral is genuinely integrable: actual signed path regret has absolute value at most T, proved from bounded squared losses, and measurable history sections yield measurable finite loss sums. No Bochner nonintegrability fallback or assumed regret certificate is used.
    Algorithm parameters
    H_n=Σ_{i=1}^n1/i and log is natural log; squared loss is (x-y)^2 without1/2. Labels0/1 are legal source [0,1] outcomes and learner outputs are real [0,1]. The deterministic intermediate expected-regret bound allows arbitrary real history outputs. The probability law/count moments are total at T0, q([])=1/2, but all lower terminals require T≥1. Regret is signed cumulative regret, never average regret, clipped regret or absolute regret. The exact shifts are H(T+1) and log(T+2).
    Regret notion
    The witness may depend on the algorithm family, its seed law and T, but never on the realized seed. There is no almost-sure, high-probability, every-seed, uniform-seed or single-infinite-sequence assertion; no sharp minimax coefficient or representation theorem for every possible randomized oracle.

For bounded measurable seed policies, proved integrability permits finite weighted sum/integral interchange. These are actual compiled proof dependencies, separate from the curated teaching route.     Factor the seed/past/current law, regroup independent blocks, and extract finite disjoint IID coordinates. This derives independence of (seed,strict past) and the current target. Restrict the generated information to the supplied subfield, then derive prediction measurability and L2 from a.s. feasibility. The jointly measurable legal-history policy instantiates this interface. The actual expected-fixed minimum and square-loss decomposition yield the same-prefix sum of mean-deviation squares.

    Model
    One probability law carries a real target stream and an arbitrary measurable private tape. Before round t, H_t is generated by the tape and the strict-past target tuple. General P_t is measurable in F_t contained in H_t; concrete P_t=pi_t(S,Y_<t).
    Assumptions
    Targets are measurable, jointly independent, identically distributed and a.s. in[0,1]. The tape is independent of the WHOLE infinite target process, not merely each target separately. General predictions are a.s. feasible. Each concrete policy is jointly measurable and feasible for EVERY seed on legal unit histories; its off-cube outputs are unrestricted. Ambient measurability, L2 and current-target independence are derived.
    Algorithm parameters
    Source rounds1..T correspond to Lean0..T-1. At t=0 the past is empty but the tape is available. T0 is an explicit empty-prefix extension. These are finite-horizon statements; no asymptotic-success, high-probability or almost-sure convergence claim.
    Regret notion
    The benchmark is min_u E[sum of fixed-comparator square losses], with u in[0,1] chosen outside expectation. It equals T Var(Y_0); it is not E[min_u sum of losses]. Expected-fixed excess for the SAME stream and prefix equals sum E[(P_t-E[Y_0])^2]>=0. Private randomness is integrated by the common law; pathwise excess need not be nonnegative.

Both endpoints, T0, legal-only feasibility and current Y_0 not in private-only H_0 are checked.     For positive T, (A_T-Tv)/T=A_T/T-v. The standard little-o quotient criterion therefore gives sublinear centered excess iff the average excess tends to zero. For the actual mean learner, source Theorem1.3 bounds loss minus the empirical hindsight minimum pathwise. That empirical minimum is at most the loss of the fixed population comparator m. Integrate this inequality using derived L2, and use expected fixed loss at m=Tv to obtain E_T<=4+4lnT even without independence. With joint IID the causal lower bound also gives E_T>=0. Sandwich E_T/T between0 and(4+4lnT)/T, whose limit is zero. Apply the same normalization adapter to obtain little-o.

    For EVERY positive prefix n≤T, assume a feasible leader w_n minimizing its prefix loss against EVERY u∈V. Induct on T: compare the previous prefix with the next feasible leader and then add the current summand. This proves the hindsight Be-the-Leader inequality; supplied minimizers do not define a causal learner. For squared loss, subtract the mean and expand; the centered cross term integrates to zero. For independent random P,Y, covariance vanishes, giving E(P−Y)^2=E(P−EY)^2+Var(Y). The actual x_0=1/2, x_t=t^{-1}Σ_{i<t}Y_i depends only on strict past. Joint target independence and measurable finite sums/division derive its independence from Y_t; measurability and bounds derive L2. Under identical laws, integrate the finite sum, substitute the one-round identity and cancel T·Var(Y_0). Every resulting mean-square term is nonnegative. The population mean is feasible and attains the variance benchmark over ALL real fixed comparators; it is an analysis witness, not a learner input. A measurable scalar policy π_t of the strict finite-history tuple is independent of the current target by disjoint-coordinate independence and composition. Its L2 square identity gives a current-round variance lower bound WITHOUT same-law. Finally divide the scalar residual by T only for T>0. This last equality is not a convergence theorem.

    For each time, choose an F_t-measurable version of the original prediction under ambient mu. Lift measurability through F_t below the seed/strict-past comap and factor it as f_t(seed,history). Clip f_t with the existing unit-interval projection to obtain pi_t on every possible input. AE feasibility makes clipping fix the original value; countable intersection gives one event for every natural time. For independence, apply the genuine measurable private-seed/strict-past producer to the version, then transport independence back to the original prediction by AE equality. For the IID loss identity, measurability and AE bounds give L2, and derived current independence removes the cross term. The population mean attains the expected fixed unit-comparator benchmark; cancel T times the common variance and sum nonnegative squared deviations. The population mean is used only in analysis. Original predictions appear on both sides, and the same infinite process is used for every natural horizon, including T0.

L2 assumes probability, measurable joint-independent targets, measurable seed independent of the WHOLE infinite target stream, and subordinate F; it requires no support, same-law or L2 premise. L3 additionally needs identical target laws and AE unit bounds for targets/predictions. Current independence, attained comparator and regret identity are derived, not supplied. The benchmark is minimum of EXPECTED fixed unit losses outside expectation, not expected hindsight minimum. No rate, asymptotic success, convergence or high-probability claim follows.

    Embed real values measurably and injectively into countably many Bool coordinates. For each coordinate, augmented measurability supplies an F-measurable representative set with ambient-mu AE equality. Its membership bits form an F-measurable code. Countable intersection makes this code equal the original real code on one full-measure event. The measurable left inverse, extended to every code, produces an actual real F-measurable version equal to the original AE. The embedding is of the real output, so Omega requires no countability or standard-Borel assumption. Apply the actual real-version producer at each natural time, obtain relative AE strong measurability, and reuse the strict-past factorization/clipping producer. Original predictions are AE in[0,1] at every time; clipping gives global feasibility on every seed/history input. One countable intersection gives one AE event for all natural times and one family before all horizons. Obtain a relative measurable version from the completed-field hypothesis. Use the actual private-seed/strict-past independence producer and AE congruence. Joint target independence and seed independence of the WHOLE infinite stream derive independence of the ORIGINAL prediction and current target. No support, same-law, boundedness or prediction-integrability assumption is needed in this independence terminal. Actual completed-information versions supply the accepted AE producer, which derives current independence and bounded L2. The population mean attains minimum EXPECTED fixed unit-comparator loss outside expectation. The common target variance cancels in cumulative expected loss, leaving the sum of original squared deviations. Original predictions appear on both sides, the same infinite process is used for all natural horizons, and T0 is an empty identity. The population mean is analysis-only; no convergence, rate, pathwise or high-probability statement follows.

    Causal realization of behavioral decision kernels

    Original at printed1,3 / PDF13,15 ↗
    Compiled locallyFive derived behavioral-kernel realization endpoints; no five printed theorem attribution. One given Markov-kernel family on generated action and strict observation histories; no reduction of every arbitrary protocol, filtration or private-state algorithm to this model. The entire observation stream is exogenous and independent of the uniform tape: arbitrary temporal dependence is allowed for realization, action-dependent adaptive environments are not covered. Conditional kernel equality is AE under the actual history marginal; every-history sampler representation is a separate conclusion. The IID expected-fixed benchmark takes the infimum of expected fixed unit losses outside expectation; no hindsight min/expectation swap, rate, convergence, pathwise or high-probability bound. Classical family selection is an existence result, not a numerical sampler.     Apply pinned Mathlib kernel randomization at every natural time and choose one jointly measurable sampler family before any observation law or horizon. Every history has the exact uniform pushforward law. Induct on the actual finite action recursion. Each step restricts both prefixes, generates prior actions and appends the current sample. Prove finite-input measurability, equality of every earlier action with the same infinite process, and pointwise nonanticipation. Independent infinite uniform coordinates give independence of the current draw from the strict past tape. The product law separates the entire observation stream from the tape. Regroup these blocks and map through the actual generated history, then through the sampler; the joint law is history marginal composed with the given kernel. Use the actual measurable generated prediction and established joint law. Conditional-distribution uniqueness identifies the kernel AE under the actual generated-history marginal, including time0. Select one sampler family first and retain its recursion, joint and conditional laws for every observation law. Under coordinate IID, same-law and AE unit observations, lift those assumptions through the product law. The concrete feasible history policy instantiates the existing IID expected-fixed excess producer at every natural horizon, including zero.

    Source theorem · faithful restatement

    Actual FTL regret and ordinary-limit semantics

    Original at printed2,4,6 / PDF14,16,18 ↗
    Compiled locallyFive derived actual FTL limit hinges, not five printed results. F1/F2 allow arbitrary real observations for algebra; unit-game feasibility is not claimed for those unbounded streams. F3/F4/F5 require one all-time unit observation stream and the same initial-half strict-past meanPredict. F4 is a limit equivalence, not unconditional existence. F5 explicitly requires empiricalMean convergence; its limit m is analysis-only, never an algorithm input. Fixed-comparator limits may be strictly negative. The existing abstract unbounded-affine counterexample does not settle bounded actual FTL; a concrete bounded oscillating-mean obstruction and all-comparator converse remain separately required source reconciliation. Five bodies and twelve nondegenerate binary canaries compiled locally; semantic and complete acceptance evidence lives in runs/online-ftl-limit-20261009 and is recorded separately.     Let Phi_T be the squared loss of the horizon empirical mean. The actual old leader minimizes the prefix of lengthT. Therefore Phi_(T+1) is at most Phi_T plus the actual next loss. Induct from the empty prefix to obtain Phi_T <= the actual FTL cumulative loss, without a supplied regret premise. Use the proved empirical-mean decomposition for positiveT, and empty sums forT0. Subtract that comparator loss from the same actual cumulative FTL loss. The minus T times squared-distance term is retained exactly. Identify the feasible interval minimum with the produced empirical mean. The actual FTL gap is nonnegative by the first endpoint and at most4+4logT by the source theorem. Divide by positiveT and squeeze between zero and a bound tending to zero. For positiveT, divide the exact comparator identity byT: normalized fixed regret equals normalized best regret minus squared distance from the empirical mean. The best term tends to zero. Subtract limits in both directions to obtain the ordinary-limit equivalence. Assume the empirical mean converges to m explicitly. Continuity gives squared-distance convergence to (u-m)^2 for every fixed realu. The exact equivalence gives fixed regret limit -(u-m)^2. This is nonpositive, so restricting comparators to[0,1] supplies the literal ordinary-limit predicate.

    Lemma 1.2: Be-the-Leader

    Lean declarationBanditRL.OnlineLearning.lemma_1_2

    Compiled

    Plain-English statement. Prefix minimizers beat the final fixed leader in cumulative loss.

    Mathematical reading. Formula renderer unavailable; readable fallback: Prefix minimizers beat the final fixed leader in cumulative loss.∑t=1Tℓt(xt∗)≤∑t=1Tℓt(xT∗)Swipe to read the full formula →
    Intuition
    Prefix minimizers beat the final fixed leader in cumulative loss.
    Why it is needed
    Be-the-Leader is a proof tool comparing supplied current-prefix hindsight minimizers with the final leader. A causal learner and its performance require the separate FTL chain.
    Place in the proof
    Orabona v10 Chapter 1, printed page 4.
    Proof and Lean reading notes
    Proof idea
    Source loss ell_(t+1) is Lean loss t; source x*_n is leader n. Lean diagonal uses leader(t+1) over rangeT; the fixed comparison uses leaderT. T1 has identical sides. Existing induction cancels the final summand, applies the previous prefix inequality, then uses prefix argmin with the feasible next/final leader. For EVERY positive prefix n<=T, supplied leader n lies in V and minimizes the prefix sum against EVERY u in V. Both membership and prefix argmin are premises; minimizer existence is not constructed. For T>0 this data implies V inhabited; T0 is a vacuous empty-sum extension with no condition on leader0.
    Lean reading notes
    The source uses a subset V of real Euclidean space and losses defined on V. Lean permits any ambient type X and total real loss functions; restricting them to V recovers the source. For every positive prefix n <= T, leader n must belong to V and minimize the prefix loss against every u in V. These minimizers are supplied; their existence is not proved. No geometry or probability assumption is needed. The leader includes the current loss, so it is a hindsight object rather than a strict-past FTL prediction. At T = 0 the conclusion is the empty-sum extension; T = 1 has identical sides. Seven named tests include changing feasible minimizers with strict inequality -2 < 0, a feasible nonoptimal sequence reversing the comparison, and an ambient-domain sequence showing why membership is necessary. The last sequence is not admissible when source losses are defined only on V.     Orabona v10 Chapter 1, printed page 4.
    Proof and Lean reading notes
    Proof idea
    Produce prefix empirical-mean minimizers, apply Be-the-Leader, derive stability from the actual mean update, and sum. The retained theorem bounds the harmonic sum by1+logT; two separate proof statements now retain the first-round quarter.
    Lean reading notes
    Positive horizon T; every target in its finite prefix belongs to [0,1]. There is no probability or global future-boundedness premise. Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. The predictor uses exactly the targets already observed: first prediction 1/2, then their empirical mean. Empty-prefix mean0 is bookkeeping and differs from the first prediction. The final empirical mean is proved feasible and globally minimizing, so its loss is the source best-fixed minimum over [0,1]. Prefix leaders are produced for Be-the-Leader; hindsight leaders are auxiliary, while predictions use the strict past. Source rounds1..T are Lean indices0..T-1. The tail range(T-1) has real denominators t+2>0 and is empty at T=1. Compiled local proof package; chapter acceptance and main integration remain separate. The arbitrary-initial FTL family and a minimax lower bound are not established by these two bounds.

    Proof and Lean reading notes
    Proof idea
    At zero the identity is y0=0+y0. At positive t, split the finite sum at t and clear the positive denominators t and t+1; elementary algebra proves the update.
    Lean reading notes
    Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. Fix initial c before observations. Lean time t counts observed labels y0,...,y(t-1); predict before observing yt, then update the local state with yt. The algebraic identities hold for all real initial values and labels. Source feasibility requires c in [0,1] and only the strict-past labels yi in [0,1] for i<t; the current and future labels are unrestricted. The state is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair (count,value). The count grows; there is no fixed-bit memory, executable implementation or runtime certificate. Strict-prefix equality compares the same fixed c and gives no causality guarantee if an external caller chooses c from future data. Six public canaries check distinct initial states and their identical first update; varying means1/2 and2/3; unchanged prediction before a changed current target and changed next state; feasible initial1 and outside-initial2 at time0; the half-state two-round regret3/4 with the prior bound; and feasible initial1,target0 giving first loss1>1/4. Compiled local BODY-approved package. Combined project, reader FINAL, native acceptance and PR delivery are separate pending gates. No new regret rate for arbitrary c. The first-round quarter and the prior refined/logarithmic theorem remain specific to c=1/2. Chapter 1 remains open: W/V action-domain mapping and the logarithmic lower-bound/source-claim audit are required, together with actual contributor reconciliation.     Plain-English statement. The all-time mean successor identity has positive real denominator t+1. At t=0 the empty empirical mean is0 but the actual prediction is c.     Rewrite the actual state by the proved identity and use predictor feasibility. Initial2 at time0 is an ambient outside-domain counterexample, rather than a source-feasible test.
    Lean reading notes
    Deterministic scalar squared-loss guessing. Fix initial c before observations. Lean time t counts observed labels y0,...,y(t-1); predict before observing yt, then update the local state with yt. The algebraic identities hold for all real initial values and labels. Source feasibility requires c in [0,1] and only the strict-past labels yi in [0,1] for i<t; the current and future labels are unrestricted. The state is a mathematical noncomputable exact-real pair (count,value). The count grows; there is no fixed-bit memory, executable implementation or runtime certificate. Strict-prefix equality compares the same fixed c and gives no causality guarantee if an external caller chooses c from future data. Six public canaries check distinct initial states and their identical first update; varying means1/2 and2/3; unchanged prediction before a changed current target and changed next state; feasible initial1 and outside-initial2 at time0; the half-state two-round regret3/4 with the prior bound; and feasible initial1,target0 giving first loss1>1/4. The first-round quarter and the prior refined/logarithmic theorem remain specific to c=1/2.     The same signed regret as a sum of gaps

    Lean declarationBanditRL.OnlineLearning.comparatorRegret_eq_sum

    Compiled

    Plain-English statement. Use Mathlib Finset.sum_sub_distrib in reverse; instantiate the common carrier with Subtype W and embed the comparator from V.

    Mathematical reading. Formula renderer unavailable; readable fallback: Use Mathlib Finset.sum_sub_distrib in reverse; instantiate the common carrier with Subtype W and embed the comparator from V.RT(u)=∑t=1T(ℓt(xt)−ℓt(u))Swipe to read the full formula →
    Intuition
    Comparison uses one supplied prediction sequence and each fixed feasible comparator.
    Why it is needed
    Keep source domains and the exact one-sided upper condition explicit in the shared library.
    Place in the proof
    Orabona v10 printedp2/PDF14, comparator definition, Remark1.1 and Footnote1; library algebraic adapter/model mapping, not a new numbered source theorem.
    Proof and Lean reading notes
    Proof idea
    Use Mathlib Finset.sum_sub_distrib in reverse; instantiate the common carrier with Subtype W and embed the comparator from V.
    Lean reading notes
    Losses are defined on W, predictions belong to W, and fixed comparators belong to V⊆W. Lean uses X=Subtype W and comparator set {w:Subtype W | w.val∈V}; inclusion embeds a subtype-V comparator without changing its value. The source uses finite-dimensional Euclidean vectors; the shared algebraic API explicitly generalizes the carrier. Footnote1 states a modelling possibility, not a generic algorithm or performance theorem. Only inclusion V⊆W is needed for the embedding. Finite regret algebra needs no convexity, compactness, probability or nonnegativity. A supplied prediction sequence is shared across every comparator. Its loss-prefix evaluation identity does not prove causal learner recomputation, future independence or existence of a best comparator. A W-loss restricts to V by pullback; a V-only loss is never evaluated outside V. Source round1 is Lean0; sums use range T. At T0 both sums are empty; Lean real division is total. Eventual atTop bounds concern sufficiently large positive horizons. Empty comparator sets give a vacuous property; supplied subtype inhabitants do not prove arbitrary sets are nonempty. NoRegret means, for each fixed feasible comparator u and every positive epsilon, normalized regret is eventually at most epsilon. The threshold may depend on u and epsilon. This is an explicit interpretation of the source displayed ordinary-limit inequality: it agrees when the ordinary limit exists, but proves no ordinary limit existence, convergence tozero, absolute bound, nonnegative regret or uniform comparator threshold. Subtract the two finite loss sums and distribute subtraction termwise using Mathlib Finset.sum_sub_distrib. For the adapter, tendsto_order makes a comparator-wise bound tending tozero less than any positive epsilon eventually; intersect this event with the supplied actual normalized-regret upper bound and use transitivity. The adapter does not itself construct that bound. The typed illustrative game has V=[0,1],W=[0,2], constant output2 and loss_t(x)=-x onW. For every comparator u∈V, each actual loss gap is u-2≤-1≤0; Finset.sum_nonpos and div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg make its finite sum and normalized regret nonpositive. The actual shared adapter applies with bound0. At T2 the same output gives regret -4 against0 and -2 against1. This is a generalized negative-regret test, separate from the source squared guessing game and no universal W performance claim. Chapter 1 remains open. This package audits the required W/V domain mapping using the existing shared Regret API; it adds zero production mathematical results or definitions. Full regret/minimum and no-regret source reconciliation, the logarithmic lower-bound/source claim and other required module audits remain open. There are16 source items but the mandatory proof total is unknown(null). Chapter2 is incomplete; Chapters3–16 are unenumerated and necessary appendices remain required. The total Goal is active.     A produced binary history law

    Lean declarationBanditRL.OnlineLearning.GuessingLower.prefix_mass_one

    Compiled

    Plain-English statement. Split each length-(T+1) vector into its newest bit and prior vector; branch weights sum to w(h), then use the same law induction.

    Mathematical reading. Formula renderer unavailable; readable fallback: Split each length-(T+1) vector into its newest bit and prior vector; branch weights sum to w(h), then use the same law induction.∑v∈{0,1}Tw(v)=1Swipe to read the full formula →
    Intuition
    The adversary law, causal learner path and hindsight mean refer to exactly the same finite binary sequence.
    Why it is needed
    Expose the actual producer supporting the required qualitative logarithmic source claim.
    Place in the proof
    Orabona v10 printed p.4/PDF p.16 states that logarithmic dependence is unavoidable and explicitly gives no minimax-optimality proof there. H(T+1)/6 and log(T+2)/6 are derived quantitative support, neither printed nor claimed sharp. This is not a numbered source theorem.
    Proof and Lean reading notes
    Proof idea
    Split each length-(T+1) vector into its newest bit and prior vector; branch weights sum to w(h), then use the same law induction.
    Lean reading notes
    Histories h are newest-first binary lists. K(h) counts true labels; q(h)=(K(h)+1)/(|h|+2), w([])=1 and w(b::h)=w(h)*(q(h) if b=true else1-q(h)). This same normalized positive binary law depends on neither learner policy nor seed. Normalization and nonnegativity are proved before constructing the shared finite-action probability measure and integral. The chronological stream is reverse(h); padding beyond its length is never used by regret. The prediction at Lean round t receives reverse of the chronological strict prefix of length t. The current label is revealed after prediction. Source round1 is Lean0. For every measurable seed space Ω, every probability measure μ, every policy A:Ω→List Bool→ℝ with each history section ω↦A(ω,h) measurable and A(ω,h)∈[0,1] for every seed and every history, and every positive natural horizon T, the terminal produces ONE binary vector v of length T outside the seed integral. The seed may encode the full private random tape; each policy remains strict-past. The integral is genuinely integrable: actual signed path regret has absolute value at most T, proved from bounded squared losses, and measurable history sections yield measurable finite loss sums. No Bochner nonintegrability fallback or assumed regret certificate is used. H_n=Σ_{i=1}^n1/i and log is natural log; squared loss is (x-y)^2 without1/2. Labels0/1 are legal source [0,1] outcomes and learner outputs are real [0,1]. The deterministic intermediate expected-regret bound allows arbitrary real history outputs. The probability law/count moments are total at T0, q([])=1/2, but all lower terminals require T≥1. Regret is signed cumulative regret, never average regret, clipped regret or absolute regret. The exact shifts are H(T+1) and log(T+2). Actual recursive normalization gives E_T[K]=T/2 and E_T[K²]=T(2T+1)/6, hence E_T[q(1-q)]=(T+3)/(6(T+2)). Causal prefix identities generate the actual same-path cumulative learner-loss successor. Conditional square loss is at least q(1-q), so summing its actual expected increments gives learner loss at least T/6+(H(T+1)-1)/6. The shared empirical mean is proved feasible and globally minimizes the same binary path square loss; its produced expected optimum is (T-1)/6. Subtracting these same-path quantities proves E_T[R_A]≥H(T+1)/6 for any real strict-history policy. For bounded measurable seed policies, proved integrability permits finite weighted sum/integral interchange. Strictly positive normalized path weights imply some ONE path has seed-average regret at least H(T+1)/6. Mathlib log_add_one_le_harmonic gives the log endpoint. These are actual compiled proof dependencies, separate from the curated teaching route. The witness may depend on the algorithm family, its seed law and T, but never on the realized seed. There is no almost-sure, high-probability, every-seed, uniform-seed or single-infinite-sequence assertion; no sharp minimax coefficient or representation theorem for every possible randomized oracle. Sixteen named canaries compile actual causality, dependent two-step weights1/3 and1/6, T0/T2 normalization, first/second count moments1 and5/3, variance5/24, actual same-path regret13/36 and optimum1/2, the one-step1/4 lower endpoint, deterministic Dirac specialization and a genuinely two-atom seed policy with different outputs0/1 and atom masses1/2. The seeded T2 harmonic endpoint is11/36. Numerical/type identity checks are validation, not substitutes for universal theorem bodies. Seventy-six named kernel checks use only standard Lean axioms;64 actual closed proposition and12 definition identities compile, with recursive/nominal equality bridges where rfl is insufficient. Thirty specified compiler VALUE pairs are checked; this is not a teaching-edge inventory. Only the required C1-LOG-UNAVOIDABLE source claim is supported by this new proof package. BODY review accepted with explicit delta; integrated root/Tests/harness, shared registry/site/pixels, FINAL review, native acceptance and PR remain separate gates.     Intuition
    Minimize expected cumulative loss over one fixed comparator; expectation stays inside that minimization. For causal predictions, derive current-target independence from the strict past.
    Why it is needed
    Connect the source expected fixed benchmark to genuine causal processes.
    Place in the proof
    Source printed1–2/PDF13–14 motivates squared loss with IID unit targets, cumulative excess (1.1) and average (1.2), and the minimum of EXPECTED FIXED cumulative loss. Eight derived producer/representation/adapters are not eight printed theorems or new rates. T0 is an explicit empty extension without uniqueness. Same-law alone suffices for fixed benchmark; deterministic measurable finite-history feasibility is required only on legal unit tuples. The broader all-strategies source claim is not closed by this package.
    Proof and Lean reading notes
    Proof idea
    Produce L2 from a.s. support and use same-law moments before finite summation.
    Lean reading notes
    On a probability space, each real observation is measurable, a.s. in[0,1], and identically distributed withY0. Produce L2 and the feasible population mean m=E[Y0], then actual IsLeast and sInf. The comparator u is chosen outside the expectation: B_T=min_{u∈[0,1]}E[Σ(u−Y_t)^2], not E[min_{u∈[0,1]}Σ(u−Y_t)^2]. Generally infinite comparator image, actual attainment established. For causal performance the targets are jointly independent. A measurable policy consumes ONLY the finite strict-past tuple i<t and is feasible on legal tuples. A.s. history support produces predictionL2 and strict-history independence produces current-target independence. Both are derived, not supplied terminal certificates. I004 is a supplied-L2/independence consumer only; I005policy and I006meanPredict are the actual producers. Bare definitions and arbitrary supplied traces do not certify causality or nonnegative excess. Actual meanPredict starts at1/2 then uses the strict-past empirical mean; the constant population mean is a distribution-known oracle, not a learner discovering an unknown law. Source rounds1..T correspond to Lean0..T−1 on the SAME prefix. T0 has empty loss/minimum0 without uniqueness; averages require T>0. Finite normalization does not establish sublinear/vanishing asymptotic success, expected convergence, high probability, or almost-sure guarantees. First prove fixed square-loss expectation decomposition, using a.s. support and same-law integral/variance equality. Produce the feasible population mean, IsLeast membership and every lower comparison BEFORE applying mathlib csInf_eq. Independence decomposes each prediction square into variance plus mean-estimation error. Finite integration/summation and the actual same-prefix benchmark yield E-fixed excess=ΣE[(P_t−m)^2]≥0 for each actual causal producer. The distribution-known constant mean attains zero; the positive-horizon average is exactly cumulative excess/T. No supplied regret/stability/argmin assumption or min/expectation interchange.     A real version from ambient null-augmented measurability

    Lean declarationBanditRL.OnlineLearning.completed_measurable_real_exists_version

    Compiled

    Plain-English statement. Embed real values measurably and injectively into countably many Bool coordinates. For each coordinate, augmented measurability supplies an F-measurable representative set with ambient-mu AE equality. Its membership bits form an F-measurable code. Countable intersection makes this code equal the original real code on one full-measure event. The measurable left inverse, extended to every code, produces an actual real F-measurable version equal to the original AE. The embedding is of the real output, so Omega requires no countability or standard-Borel assumption.
